question.text: Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) valuation is most appropriate for:

answer.text: Single-product companies operating in one industry
Clustered or bundled businesses, such as ITC or L&T, that have distinct business verticals which are best valued separately and then summed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XV (p.213), clustered or bundled businesses such as ITC and L&T are best valued by valuing each business vertical separately and adding the valuations together — the Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) method. The Trap: Single-product companies operating in one industry do not require SOTP; a single valuation method on the consolidated entity is sufficient. Bonds and money market instruments are valued using interest-rate-based pricing methods, not SOTP. Note: SOTP is fundamentally an additive method — value each segment using the most appropriate technique for that segment, then sum.
